newsitem.title: USA: U.S., India seek to gloss over diplomats row.
newsitem.headline: U.S., India seek to gloss over diplomats row.

text.p: The United States on Tuesday joined India in calling for a new effort to improve relations despite an intelligence row which led to a mutual expulsion of diplomats.
"We hope that these events can be put behind us and that our governments can get on with the very important business of strengthening our relationship," State Department spokesman Glyn Davies said.
"India is the world's largest democracy. We are the world's most powerful. And it's important that India and the United States move on from here," he told a news briefing.

The State Department said on Sunday it had ordered two Indian diplomats -- consular officers in San Francisco and Chicago -- to leave the country in retaliation for the expulsion of a U.S. official from New Delhi last month.
India said on Monday it regretted the U.S. decision but would still work with Washington to improve friendly relations.
Indian officials said the expelled U.S. diplomat had established unauthorized contacts with Rattan Sehgal, head of the anti-espionage division of India's Intelligence Bureau.
Sehgal was asked to resign after the alleged links were discovered.
Davies said the two Indians who were expelled had engaged in "activities incompatible with their consular status" -- a catch-all formula often employed in such cases.
Davies said he "wouldn't call this a diplomatic war" but "kind of a one-off incident".
"Our understanding is that New Delhi shares our wish to move on from here and put this behind us, and so that's what we're going to do," he said.
